messages.author: fc0d70eb69cd4471
messages.subject: R cannot open file with cfa()
parts:
Dear all, 

I m using cfa to complete my analysis,Until yesterday, I got the result. At the present time, this error message appears :"No such file or directory" and I don't know why. I removed all theextra white space and restarted again R but that doesn't solve my problem.

code using : 
 model8='
#latent variable 
health_L=~health_cat+cat_time_hosp+cat_night_hosp+cat_annuel
# Regression operator
Health_L~a*gender_cat+n*status_cat+e*age_div+m*owners+i*natio_cat+k*income
#Meditor
status_cat~d*age_div+g*natio_cat+b*gender_cat 
owners~c*gender_cat+f*age_div+h*natio_cat+l*status_cat+j*income 
# covariance 
health_cat~~cat_time_hosp
health_cat~~cat_night_hosp
cat_time_hosp~~cat_night_hosp
age_div~~natio_cat 
gender_cat~~natio_cat
age_div~~gender_cat
#Correlation
income~~natio_cat
income~~age_div
income~~gender_cat
#indirect effect: 
# Marital_status:
bn:=b*n # Gender
dn:=d*n #Age
gn:=g*n #Nationality
#Owners:
cm:=c*m #gendre
fm:=f*m #Age 
hm:=h*m #nationality
jm:=j*m #Income
#matial_status/owners:
blm:=b*l*m #gender
dlm:=d*l*m #Age
glm:=g*l*m #nationality
#Totaleffect
total:=a+e+n+m+i+k+(b*n)+(d*n)+(g*n)+(c*m)+(f*m)+(h*m)+(j*m)+(b*l*m)+(d*l*m)+(g*l*m)
'
model.fit8<-cfa(model8,data=data,estimator = "DWLS",se = "robust",test = "scaled.shifted")

error message: 
> model.fit8<-cfa(model8,data=data,estimator = "DWLS",se = "robust",test = "scaled.shifted")

In addition: Warning message:

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: R cannot open file with cfa()
parts:
No idea what is going on. Most likely, this is not related to lavaan.
Just 3 suggestions:

1) use lavaan::cfa() instead of cfa() to make sure you are calling
lavaan's cfa()

2) type at the R console

sink()

to make sure no connections are still open.

3) open vanilla R (not RStudio) and try it there

Yves.

Hm. lavaan has trouble computing the 'A1' matrix (which is the

right. Would you be able to send me your data (or a snippet of the data,
just enough to reproduce this), and your full R script?

Yves.
